This document reproduces the parts of the paper that concern the full sample and
the male and female models. The model for immature animals, the year-effect figures
and the remaining tables and figures are produced by the scripts in `R/` (see the
README). Run it from the project root; everything it writes goes to `output/`.

## Setup

```{r setup}
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(sf)
library(INLA)

dir.create("output", showWarnings = FALSE)

thresholds    <- c(17, 41)  # toxicity thresholds, mg/kg lipid weight
prob_level    <- 0.8        # threshold year = first year with P(mean < threshold) >= 0.8
n_samples     <- 2000       # posterior samples for the projections
run_selection <- FALSE      # TRUE refits all 112 candidate models per sex (slow)

sex_cols <- c("Males" = "#55A868", "Females" = "#4C72B0", "Pregnant females" = "#FDD9A2")
```

```{r data}
pcb <- read.csv("data/PCBcorrectedDB.csv", sep = ";") |>
  mutate(
    Country_Code = factor(Country_Code, levels = c(4, 5), labels = c("France", "Spain")),
    Sex          = factor(Sex, levels = 1:3,
                          labels = c("Males", "Females", "Pregnant females")),
    Maturity     = factor(Maturity, levels = 0:2,
                          labels = c("Immatures", "Matures", "PregnantMatures"))
  )

males   <- pcb |> filter(Sex == "Males") |> droplevels()
females <- pcb |> filter(Sex != "Males") |> droplevels()
```

The response in every model is `ICES73`, the Aroclor 1254-equivalent concentration
(sum of the seven ICES indicator congeners × 3, mg/kg lipid weight).

## 1. Descriptive statistics (Table 2)

```{r table2}
table2 <- pcb |>
  mutate(Maturity = if_else(Maturity == "Immatures", "Immatures", "Matures")) |>
  group_by(Country = Country_Code, Sex, Maturity) |>
  summarise(
    n              = n(),
    n_above_17     = sum(ICES73 > 17),
    n_above_41     = sum(ICES73 > 41),
    sum18_mean     = mean(sum18PCB),
    sum18_median   = median(sum18PCB),
    ICES7_mean     = mean(ICES7),
    ICES7_median   = median(ICES7),
    Aroclor_mean   = mean(ICES73),
    Aroclor_median = median(ICES73),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(across(where(is.double), ~ round(.x, 2)))

write.csv(table2, "output/table2_summary.csv", row.names = FALSE)
knitr::kable(table2)
```

Percentage of each sex above the thresholds (as reported in the Results):

```{r exceedance}
pcb |>
  group_by(Sex) |>
  summarise(n = n(),
            pct_above_17 = round(100 * mean(ICES73 > 17), 1),
            pct_above_41 = round(100 * mean(ICES73 > 41), 1)) |>
  knitr::kable()
```

## 2. Map of strandings (Figure 1)

The two panels below are the base layers of Figure 1; the final layout (inset,
mass-stranding markers) was assembled by hand. The GADM shapefiles have to be
downloaded first (see the README).

```{r map}
countries <- do.call(rbind, lapply(c("ESP", "FRA", "GBR", "PRT"), function(iso)
  read_sf(sprintf("data/shapefiles/gadm36_%s_0.shp", iso))))
strandings <- st_as_sf(pcb, coords = c("Lon", "Lat"), crs = st_crs(countries))

map_country <- function(country, margin = 0.3) {
  pts <- filter(strandings, Country_Code == country)
  bb  <- st_bbox(pts)
  ggplot() +
    geom_sf(data = countries, fill = "grey90", colour = "grey40", linewidth = 0.2) +
    geom_sf(data = pts, aes(colour = Sex), size = 2.5, alpha = 0.8) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = sex_cols, drop = FALSE) +
    coord_sf(xlim = bb[c("xmin", "xmax")] + c(-margin, margin),
             ylim = bb[c("ymin", "ymax")] + c(-margin, margin)) +
    theme_bw() +
    theme(panel.grid = element_blank())
}

for (country in levels(pcb$Country_Code)) {
  p <- map_country(country)
  print(p)
  ggsave(sprintf("output/map_%s.svg", tolower(country)), p, width = 6, height = 6)
}
```

## 3. Model selection (Supplementary Tables S2–S3)

Gamma models with a log link were fitted for every combination of the candidate
terms in four sets, which gives 112 models per sex, and compared by WAIC and LCPO
(LCPO = −Σ log CPO). The results used in the paper are stored in
`data/unique_models{m,f}.rds` and summarised by `R/01_model_selection_tables.R`.
Set `run_selection <- TRUE` above to refit them; the new tables are written to
`output/` and do not overwrite the published ones.

```{r selection}
candidate_terms <- list(
  linear      = c("Country_Code", "Year", "Length", "Maturity"),
  year_rw2    = c("Country_Code", "f(Year, model = 'rw2')",
                  "f(Month, model = 'rw2', cyclic = TRUE)", "Length", "Maturity"),
  length_rw2  = c("Country_Code", "f(Year, model = 'rw2')",
                  "f(Month, model = 'rw2', cyclic = TRUE)", "f(Length, model = 'rw2')",
                  "Maturity"),
  year_iid    = c("Country_Code", "f(Year, model = 'iid')",
                  "f(Month, model = 'rw2', cyclic = TRUE)", "f(Length, model = 'rw2')",
                  "Maturity")
)

# every combination of a set of terms, as formula strings
all_formulas <- function(terms) {
  unlist(lapply(0:length(terms), function(m) {
    if (m == 0) return("ICES73 ~ 1")
    paste("ICES73 ~ 1 +", apply(combn(terms, m), 2, paste, collapse = " + "))
  }))
}

fit_criteria <- function(formula, data) {
  fit <- try(inla(as.formula(formula), family = "gamma", data = data,
                  control.compute = list(dic = TRUE, waic = TRUE, cpo = TRUE),
                  control.inla = list(strategy = "simplified.laplace")),
             silent = TRUE)
  if (inherits(fit, "try-error"))
    return(data.frame(Formula = formula, DIC = NA, WAIC = NA, LCPO = NA))
  data.frame(Formula = formula, DIC = fit$dic$dic, WAIC = fit$waic$waic,
             LCPO = -sum(log(fit$cpo$cpo), na.rm = TRUE))
}

select_models <- function(data) {
  formulas <- unique(unlist(lapply(candidate_terms, all_formulas)))
  do.call(rbind, lapply(formulas, fit_criteria, data = data)) |> arrange(WAIC)
}

if (run_selection) {
  saveRDS(select_models(males),   "output/model_selection_males.rds")
  saveRDS(select_models(females), "output/model_selection_females.rds")
}
```

## 4. Final models (Table 3)

Males: country, maturity and a smooth (RW2) effect of year. Females: country and
maturity status (immature, mature non-pregnant, pregnant).

```{r final-models}
fit_males <- inla(ICES73 ~ Country_Code + Maturity + f(Year, model = "rw2"),
                  family = "gamma", data = males,
                  control.compute = list(dic = TRUE, waic = TRUE, cpo = TRUE))

fit_females <- inla(ICES73 ~ Country_Code + Maturity,
                    family = "gamma", data = females,
                    control.compute = list(dic = TRUE, waic = TRUE, cpo = TRUE))

fixed_effects <- function(fit, model) {
  s <- fit$summary.fixed
  data.frame(Model = model, Parameter = rownames(s), Mean = s$mean, SD = s$sd,
             Lower_95 = s$`0.025quant`, Upper_95 = s$`0.975quant`)
}

table3 <- rbind(fixed_effects(fit_males, "Males"),
                fixed_effects(fit_females, "Females")) |>
  mutate(across(Mean:Upper_95, ~ round(.x, 2)))

write.csv(table3, "output/table3_males_females.csv", row.names = FALSE)
knitr::kable(table3, row.names = FALSE)
```

## 5. Projections for males (Figure 4a, Supplementary Figures S1–S2)

The male model is refitted with empty rows for 2020–2075, so INLA extrapolates the
year effect. Joint posterior samples of the linear predictor give the distribution
of the mean concentration in each year, country and maturity class.

```{r projections}
future <- expand.grid(Year         = 2020:2075,
                      Country_Code = levels(males$Country_Code),
                      Maturity     = levels(males$Maturity)) |>
  mutate(ICES73 = NA_real_)

males_aug <- bind_rows(males, future)
pred_rows <- which(is.na(males_aug$ICES73))

fit_proj <- inla(ICES73 ~ Country_Code + Maturity + f(Year, model = "rw2"),
                 family = "gamma", data = males_aug,
                 control.predictor = list(compute = TRUE, link = 1),
                 control.compute   = list(config = TRUE))

samples <- inla.posterior.sample(n_samples, fit_proj, seed = 1)
eta <- sapply(samples, function(s) s$latent[paste0("Predictor:", pred_rows), 1])
mu  <- exp(eta)   # rows = future year x country x maturity, columns = samples

projection <- future |>
  select(Year, Country_Code, Maturity) |>
  mutate(median     = apply(mu, 1, median),
         lower_95   = apply(mu, 1, quantile, 0.025),
         upper_95   = apply(mu, 1, quantile, 0.975),
         p_below_17 = rowMeans(mu < thresholds[1]),
         p_below_41 = rowMeans(mu < thresholds[2]))

write.csv(projection, "output/projection_males.csv", row.names = FALSE)
```

Year in which each group falls below each threshold:

```{r threshold-years}
first_year <- function(year, p) if (any(p >= prob_level)) min(year[p >= prob_level]) else NA

threshold_years <- projection |>
  group_by(Country_Code, Maturity) |>
  summarise(below_17 = first_year(Year, p_below_17),
            below_41 = first_year(Year, p_below_41),
            .groups = "drop")

write.csv(threshold_years, "output/threshold_years_males.csv", row.names = FALSE)
knitr::kable(threshold_years)
```

```{r figure-4a}
fig4a <- ggplot(projection, aes(Year, median, colour = Country_Code)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lower_95, ymax = upper_95, fill = Country_Code),
              alpha = 0.15, colour = NA) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.9) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = thresholds, linetype = "dashed", colour = "red") +
  facet_wrap(~ Maturity) +
  scale_y_log10() +
  scale_colour_brewer(palette = "Dark2") +
  scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Pastel2") +
  labs(y = "Predicted PCB concentration (mg/kg lw)", colour = NULL, fill = NULL) +
  theme_bw()

print(fig4a)
ggsave("output/projection_males.png", fig4a, width = 10, height = 4.2, dpi = 300)
```

```{r figures-s1-s2}
probability_plot <- function(threshold) {
  p_col  <- paste0("p_below_", threshold)
  y_col  <- paste0("below_", threshold)
  cross  <- filter(threshold_years, !is.na(.data[[y_col]]))
  ggplot(projection, aes(Year, .data[[p_col]])) +
    geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = prob_level, linetype = "dashed") +
    geom_vline(data = cross, aes(xintercept = .data[[y_col]]),
               colour = "#33CC33", linetype = "dashed") +
    geom_text(data = cross, aes(x = .data[[y_col]], y = 0.03, label = .data[[y_col]]),
              colour = "#33CC33", angle = 90, hjust = 0, vjust = -0.4) +
    facet_grid(Maturity ~ Country_Code) +
    scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 1), breaks = seq(0, 1, 0.25)) +
    labs(y = sprintf("P(mean < %d mg/kg lw)", threshold)) +
    theme_bw() +
    theme(strip.background = element_rect(fill = "grey90"),
          strip.text = element_text(face = "bold"))
}

for (threshold in thresholds) {
  p <- probability_plot(threshold)
  print(p)
  ggsave(sprintf("output/probability_below_%d_males.png", threshold), p,
         width = 8, height = 5, dpi = 300)
}
```
